description: One authorized Collab stewardship patrol activation reads current role, task, capacity, worktree, resource, P0/P1, and issue facts; classifies actionable work and protected holds; then routes by work horizon, not by a peer-first rule: a durable long-horizon subgoal goes to an available authorized peer that owns that subgoal as its own orchestrator, while one-shot execution or observation goes to a `codex exec --profile gcm` subworker (the declared host fallback applies only when gcm is unavailable). A peer is not a universal first hop and is not a direct execution worker; the master does not take over a peer's goal. Execute through the public board or the one-shot worker; verify behavior and closure or an explicit park; then make one final scheduling decision: re-arm one consumed one-shot goal/deadline occurrence with `appsdk goal subscribe`, or reconcile the owned goal/task to ended when no actionable work remains. Every failure or ambiguous ownership state reaches the same result sink without becoming success. Direct-message reception is daemon-owned and never closed by patrol termination.

nodes.description: Choose the owner by work horizon and authority: a durable long-horizon subgoal goes to an available authorized peer that is the orchestrator of that subgoal, not a direct worker; one-shot execution or observation goes to a `codex exec --profile gcm` subworker, with the declared host fallback only when gcm is unavailable. No peer-first universal rule and no private-child fallback path. Missing capacity or authority is an explicit hold, not a silent re-route.

Final owned-scheduling decision. When actionable scheduling remains, re-arm exactly one bounded one-shot goal/deadline occurrence through the existing goal owner; otherwise reconcile the owned goal/task to ended so its finite patrol stops. Neither branch controls the daemon-owned default direct-message base reception.
